range: f283a5a -- specs/requests/02-client-participants.md (the only change since the fix pass; git diff HEAD is empty)
request: Client participants: let a client contact hold a principal in an organization and take part in requests raised for their client, without becoming a member of the organization.

findings.claim: Requirement 19a decides what invitation time inspects on the ClientMembership side but leaves the Membership side undecided for a client invitation: whether the inherited alreadyMember refusal fires when role = 'client'. One reading makes edge case 1 and TC-02-INT-03 unreachable.

witness.detail: Requirement 19a (:227): 'Invitation time inspects no ClientMembership. Spec 03's alreadyMember refusal — 400 INVITE_MESSAGES.alreadyMember — reads active Membership rows only, and this spec adds no counterpart for ClientMembership.' It says which rows the check reads, never which invitations it applies to. The POST /api/invitations contract (:522) says 'everything else exactly as spec 03 defines it', and apps/api/src/invitations/invitations.service.ts:92-97 runs that check for every role before any role branch: 'const invitee = await this.prisma.account.findUnique({ where: { email }, include: { memberships: { where: { organizationId: caller.organizationId, status: active } } } }); if (invitee && invitee.memberships.length > 0) throw new BadRequestException({ message: INVITE_MESSAGES.alreadyMember });'. Reading A — the check applies to role = 'client' too — makes it impossible ever to mint a client invitation for an address that holds an active Membership, so edge case 1 (:581) 'An address that is already an active staff member accepts a client invitation | 409 accountIsStaff. No ClientMembership; the invitation stays pending' is unreachable and TC-02-INT-03 (:891) 'Accept a client invitation with an address that is already an active staff member' cannot reach its state: the mint answers 400 alreadyMember. Reading B — the check is skipped for a client invitation — runs both, and is what the new Error Messages row (:657) implies by scoping the message to 'An address that already holds an active Membership is invited as staff'. The two readings differ by a status, a message and the existence of an invitation row.

findings.suggestedFix: In requirement 19a, say whether the alreadyMember refusal fires for role = 'client'. The table row at :657 and edge case 1 both point one way: a client invitation for an address that holds an active Membership is minted and mailed, and the refusal is the accept transaction's 409 accountIsStaff — state that sentence in 19a, and keep the row's 'invited as staff' scoping.

findings.claim: Requirement 2 states the accept-time refusal only for an active row of the other kind, while requirement 19a, edge case 21 and TC-02-INT-16 all require a refusal for a same-kind acceptance — an account already holding an active ClientMembership accepting a further client invitation.

witness.detail: Requirement 2 (:77): 'the accept-invitation handler re-reads both inside its transaction and refuses when an active row of the other kind already exists, with 409 and CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.accountIsStaff or …accountIsClient.' Requirement 19a (:231): 'an address that already holds an active ClientMembership can be minted a client invitation and a staff invitation alike, each succeeding, and the refusal comes at acceptance: 409 accountIsClient (requirement 2).' For a client invitation there is no active row of the other kind, so requirement 2's condition never fires; the data model's ClientMembership.accountId @unique is what stops the insert, and the spec never says what that answers except in 19a and TC-02-INT-16. The rule is stated, but not where the mechanism is.

findings.suggestedFix: Extend requirement 2's mechanism sentence: the accept handler refuses when an active row of either kind already exists for the account — the other kind with accountIsStaff/accountIsClient as today, and a second active ClientMembership with 409 accountIsClient.

findings.claim: TC-02-INT-12 does not say when the second request is created. Created after the removal, as the step order reads, it cannot be addressed to that client user at all.

witness.detail: TC-02-INT-12 (:972): 'address a request to the first on a project of that client, then remove that user. Reassign the request to a member. Then repeat on a second request in the same state…'. Requirement 27 (:268): 'Only an active client user of an active client may be chosen. A removed user … is 400 with REQUEST_MESSAGES.clientUserUnavailable', and edge case 15 (:595) says the same; state machine invariant 2 gives no restore path. So the second request must have been created before the removal, which the steps never say.

findings.suggestedFix: Say it in the steps: address two requests to the first client user, then remove them, then reassign one to a member and the other to the client's second active client user.

findings.claim: The sidebar row's absolute — sidebar-requests-link is the only navigation data-testid in the sidebar — does not say whether the Requests badge counts, and a client user is exactly the caller who has work waiting.

witness.detail: The row (:664): 'sidebar-requests-link is the only navigation data-testid in the sidebar, and every other navigation id the sidebar can draw is absent from the DOM'. apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx:84-90 draws the Requests entry with badge and badgeTestId 'sidebar-requests-badge', and apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx:45 feeds it from GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests — a route requirement 30 lets a client user call, returning the non-terminal requests addressed to them. Read strictly, the rule requires the badge suppressed for a client principal; read as nav rows only, it stays. No case in this spec settles it.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a clause to that row saying whether the Requests row carries its pending badge for a client principal, and scope the absolute to navigation destinations.

findings.claim: The new Decided block fixes which 403 a refused caller meets but not whether that 403 precedes the shape refusal, and TC-02-INT-02's new step does not say whether its client body carries a clientId.

witness.detail: A caller holding role 'user' posts { role: 'client' } with no clientId. Requirement 16 (:216): 'role = client requires clientId; any other role requires it to be absent. Both are rejected with 400 and CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.invitationShapeInvalid.' The Decided block (:524): 'the refusal a caller without permission meets is chosen by the role in the body … role = client answers 403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden.' Both outcomes — 400 invitationShapeInvalid and 403 manageForbidden — satisfy the text, and TC-02-INT-02's fourth step (:881) 'as a user, with role=client' does not say which body it sends, where its neighbours name the clientId explicitly.

findings.suggestedFix: Say in the Decided block that the permission refusal is chosen and returned before the body's shape is validated, and name the clientId in TC-02-INT-02's fourth step.
